questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following types of information systems.

(a) TPS (2 marks)

(b) MIS (2 marks)

(c) Expert system. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) TPS - Transaction Processing System (2 marks).** A TPS is an information system that **records and processes the routine day-to-day transactions of an organisation** (sales, purchases, payments, payroll, bookings, bank deposits and withdrawals) quickly and accurately, in batches or in real time. It works at the operational level and supplies the data for other systems. *Examples:* a supermarket point-of-sale system, an ATM, an airline reservation system.

**(b) MIS - Management Information System (2 marks).** An MIS is an information system that **takes the data collected by the transaction processing systems and produces summarised reports** (periodic and exception reports) that **help middle managers to monitor performance, plan and take decisions**. *Examples:* monthly sales reports, stock level reports, budget against actual spending reports.

**(c) Expert system (2 marks).** An expert system is a computer program that **stores the knowledge and rules of human experts in a particular field (a knowledge base) and uses an inference engine to reason with them**, so that it can give advice, diagnose problems or make decisions like an expert. *Examples:* medical diagnosis, fault finding in machines, assessing a loan application.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Explain the term "digital divide". (1 mark)

(b) Is digital divide experienced among the students population? Explain your answer. (2 marks)

(c) Explain two ways digital divide can be reduced in Schools. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Digital divide (1 mark).** The digital divide is the **gap between the people (or regions, or countries) who have access to ICT - computers, the Internet, mobile networks - and the skills to use it, and those who do not**.

**(b) Digital divide among students (2 marks).** **Yes**, the digital divide exists among students. Some students have their own computer or smartphone, electricity and cheap Internet access at home, while others have no device, no reliable electricity or no data bundle; students in towns and in private schools usually have better access than those in villages and in poorly equipped public schools. Students also differ in their ICT skills, and this affects their ability to research, to do assignments and to learn online.

**(c) Two ways of reducing the digital divide in schools (2 marks)** (any two, each explained):

- **Equip schools with computer laboratories and Internet access** (and a reliable power supply, for example solar panels), so that all students can use ICT at school even if they have none at home.
- **Teach ICT skills to students and teachers** by including ICT in the timetable and training the staff, so that everyone can use the equipment well.
- **Make equipment and data cheaper:** donations or loans of computers and tablets, school and community e-learning centres, and low-cost Internet bundles for students.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The Web is one of the services available on the Internet.

(a) Differentiate between the Internet and Web. (2 marks)

(b) Describe three other services available on the Internet. (3 marks)

(c) Describe E-Governance. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Internet and Web (2 marks).**

| | Internet | Web (World Wide Web) |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | The **worldwide network of interconnected computer networks** (the hardware, cables and protocols such as TCP/IP). | A **collection of linked web pages and documents** (hypertext) stored on web servers. |
| How it is used | It carries many services: e-mail, file transfer, the Web and others. | It is **only one of the services** of the Internet: pages are read with a **web browser** using HTTP and URLs. |

The Web therefore runs on the Internet; the Internet is bigger than the Web.

**(b) Three other services available on the Internet (3 marks, one mark each)** (any three):

- **E-mail:** sending and receiving electronic messages and attached files.
- **File transfer (FTP) and cloud storage:** uploading and downloading files to and from servers.
- **Voice and video communication and instant messaging (VoIP):** calls, video calls and chat (for example WhatsApp, Skype).
- **Online banking and e-commerce:** paying bills, transferring money and buying or selling goods online.
- **Streaming and forums:** watching or listening to media in real time, and discussion groups.

**(c) E-Governance (1 mark).** E-governance is the **use of ICT (websites, the Internet and mobile services) by the government to provide information and public services to citizens, businesses and its own departments** in a faster, cheaper and more transparent way, for example online payment of taxes, online registration of businesses, e-visa applications and online publication of examination results.
